<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with disciplined structure, direct A1:/A2: answers, and genuine comparative weighing. CON's strongest route was the substitution/reclassification attack ("PRO regulates the reveal; I regulate the money"), which repeatedly exploited PRO's concession that a £15 fixed-price skin is "ordinary commerce," and the Pokémon collapse, which did force PRO off its clean "money in, chance out, variable prize" definition. But PRO absorbed both hits with principled answers rather than evasion: it accepted the corner-shop line honestly and grounded the distinction in friction, unlimited 24/7 one-tap access, and per-player tuning, then reframed the harm as decision-making under engineered uncertainty rather than magnitude of spend ("fixed prices are bounded by wanting; the box is bounded by nothing"). That reframe survives CON's claim that identical spend means identical harm, which CON asserted rather than supported. PRO also landed the more damaging structural pressure: CON's own remedies (spend caps, forced odds, no one-tap) are gambling-style regulation that equally require knowing the account belongs to a minor, so the only real residual difference is whether an enforcer can fine and audit versus "the honour system we have had for a decade." CON's signalling-vs-verification reply was plausible but thin, and CON never explained why the two regimes are exclusive. PRO's repeated clipping (four turns) is a real execution cost that cost it several closing payoffs, which keeps the margin narrow rather than clear.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's slot-token pressure question and its follow-through: CON answered that a token is a "sham" existing solely to dodge the law while duplicates convert to dust or coins, and PRO turned that directly — duplicate-to-dust conversion exists precisely to keep the child spinning so the loss never feels final, so anti-avoidance logic cuts against CON's own stake test. That exchange neutralized CON's central "you always receive the product" definitional defense while using CON's own principle against him.</best_rebuttal>
